column8: Campus Commons fellows are encouraged to participate in a research partnership between The Bronfman Fellowship and CASJE (Collaborative for Applied Studies in Jewish Education) at The George Washington University. Study participants will fill out a short form and participate in one or two interviews, with an opportunity to earn up to $100. The study will explore Jewish undergraduate bridge-builders’ experiences on campus, and how Jewish identity relates to bridge-building work. The study will be conducted by Dr. Elana Riback Rand, a post-doctoral research fellow at CASJE. You can email Elana at elana.rand@gwu.edu for any questions.This study is completely separate from your Campus Commons fellowship. You are under no obligation to participate in the study. column54: I have struggled, in large part, with self-effacing behavior as a mediator or moderator in more-contentious conversations. I'm able to hold space for a variety of people with very strong, and often mutually contradictory, convictions, yet often hesitate to divulge many of my own. In part, I have adopted this position in order to best preserve my (real or perceived) impartiality as a moderator, but it has contributed to some particular fatigue. I think that I was fairly forthcoming in my conversations around my oscillating opinions on Israel/Palestine in particular, but I was nonetheless more equivocal in the way that I expressed my views than they actually perhaps were in reality. Overall, I didn't feel that I was being pressured by other students or staff at all, but rather this was an internal struggle that I think that I made progress in overcoming over the course of both the retreat and the semester as a whole.
